infra-context · generated 2026-11-10

Infra map: Bunkai

How the system under test (upex-bunkai-tms) is built and what budgets it must hold. Paths are relative to the target repo. Counts come from rg and fd sweeps and are approximate where stated. Nothing here was measured at runtime.

Overview

A Next.js 15 App Router monolith. A thin route layer under app/api/v1/ (111 route.ts files) sits over a domain-grouped lib/, and Postgres on Supabase is the authorization and business-rule layer: row-level security plus bunkai_* SQL functions (about 103 .rpc( call sites outside tests). lib/api/principal.ts states that handlers do not re-implement access checks in TypeScript. It deploys as serverless route handlers on Vercel with two Vercel crons and three pg_cron jobs.

Architecture

Dependency direction: app/* and components/* call lib/*, which calls Supabase (RLS tables and RPCs). Aliases @lib/*, @app/*, @components/* are in tsconfig.json.

API request path

  1. middleware.ts refreshes the cookie session.
  2. withApiHandler is mandatory and forces one of four postures: public, cookie-only, authenticated or required (with a non-empty capability list). A scanner test fails on an ungated route (lib/api/route-posture-scan.test.ts).
  3. A request id is read from x-request-id or minted, and echoed on the response.
  4. Identity: an Authorization: Bearer header goes to the PAT path; otherwise the SSR cookie is read and a missing user gives 401.
  5. PAT path: token format bk_pat_<prefix>.<rest>; lookup by prefix; SHA-256 comparison against a separate secrets table; revoked and expired tokens rejected; every failure is a uniform 401.
  6. For a PAT, a 60-second HS256 JWT with sub = the user id is minted and used by an anon-key client, so RLS applies the same to PAT and cookie callers (ADR-0001 of the target).
  7. Capability gate: atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin. A cookie session holds all; a PAT holds its own scopes and is bound to its token's workspace.
  8. Idempotency, where a route uses it: Idempotency-Key header (^[\w-]{8,128}$), payload hash, key stored per user, endpoint and key. Replay returns the stored result; a different payload or a pending claim returns 409.
  9. Errors use one envelope: { error: { code, message, details?, request_id? } }; a zod failure is 422 validation_failed; anything else is 500 internal_error. Success returns the resource without a wrapper.
  10. One JSON access-log line per request on stdout.

Authentication flows

  1. Password sign-up with email OTP: check-email (rate-limited), signup, confirm (verify OTP), resend. The admin auto-confirm path was removed (target ADR-0007).
  2. Password sign-in: POST /api/v1/auth/signin uses Supabase signInWithPassword, returns a uniform 401 on failure, and also mints a PAT (default name cli-signin).
  3. Magic link: magic-link sends the link with shouldCreateUser: false; app/auth/callback verifies the token hash and redirects to a safe internal path. It is stateless, so it works across devices.
  4. OAuth (GitHub, Google): PKCE plus an app-owned CSRF bk_oauth_state cookie checked on the callback (a mismatch returns 403 OAUTH_STATE_MISMATCH). Supabase links identities by verified email.
  5. PAT: POST /api/v1/tokens is cookie-only, so a PAT cannot mint a PAT. Issuance is role-gated and no global workspace:admin token exists.
  6. Sign-out is client-side (supabase.auth.signOut()); there is no app-owned logout route.

Authorization and database

  • Workspace roles viewer, member, admin, owner; RLS helpers bunkai_is_workspace_member, bunkai_can_write_workspace, bunkai_is_workspace_admin, bunkai_is_workspace_owner (supabase/migrations/0005_rls_helpers.sql).
  • Approximate counts in migrations: 152 create policy, 51 enable row level security, 298 security definer lines. The target's ADR-0012 (Proposed) requires each definer function to bind auth.uid() and scope its results, because RLS does not apply inside them.
  • The service-role client is limited to token lookup, idempotency, PAT minting, the rate-limit function, cron routes, storage operations, the Stripe webhook, the Jira import runner, data export and invite accept.
  • QA database roles qa_inspector_ro and qa_inspector_rw are created NOLOGIN in migration 0085; scripts/provision-qa-roles.ts finishes their provisioning from .env names.
  • Only datastore: Supabase Postgres, through PostgREST and RPCs. Realtime is in use (migrations 0043, 0053, 0104, 0119, 0120). Run evidence sits in a private storage bucket with a cleanup queue (migration 0097). Workspace Jira credentials are kept in Supabase Vault (0119, 0120).
  • Subsystem grouping of the migrations: tenancy and membership; projects, modules, stories and criteria; ATC authoring; tests and test plans; runs, evidence and flakiness; reports and coverage; bugs, activity, notifications and chat; identity and idempotency; billing; workspace lifecycle, export, Jira connection and QA roles. Tables and lifecycles belong to the business-data-context map (not generated yet).

Crons, system principal and internal routes

  • Vercel crons: GET /api/v1/admin/send-digest daily 08:00 and GET /api/v1/admin/storage-cleanup daily 03:00. Both use gateway posture public plus a manual CRON_SECRET bearer check (target ADR-0017, Proposed). Both verbs are exported because a POST-only route would silently 405 the cron.
  • pg_cron: bunkai-sweep-abandoned-runs every 15 minutes (0075), bunkai-sweep-rate-limit-hits hourly (0103), bunkai-purge-deleted-workspaces daily 03:00 (0084).
  • Other non-standard routes: billing/webhook (Stripe, signature only), health, the API index, /api/openapi, /api/docs.

Security architecture, performance hooks

  • Passwords are never stored by the app; Supabase Auth owns them. PATs are stored as SHA-256 hashes in a separate table so QA roles cannot read them.
  • Open-redirect guard safeInternalPath (lib/urls.ts); ESLint bans auth.getUser() inside app/api/** in favor of the gateway.
  • Keyset pagination (lib/pagination/keyset-cursor.ts, migration 0098); targeted indexes (0059 to 0061); static, cached OpenAPI route.

ADRs

The target keeps its own .context/ADR/ (42 files, two numbering streams that collide for 0002 to 0015, 0017, 0018 and 0019). Product ADRs cited above: 0001, 0002, 0005, 0006, 0007, 0008, 0010, 0012, 0014, 0017, 0019, 0025, 0026. Several shipped decisions are still marked Proposed (0012, 0017, 0019, 0021 to 0024).

This repo's own ADRs seeded by this phase (test architecture, discovered, Proposed): .context/ADR/ADR-0027-db-integration-tests-run-against-a-real-supabase.md and .context/ADR/ADR-0028-data-testid-is-the-selector-contract.md.

QA relevance

  • Test the gateway postures per route and the PAT-versus-cookie parity; test RLS isolation per role and per workspace.
  • Idempotency (replay, conflict, pending), the OAuth state check and the cron bearer check are high-value negative cases.
  • Environment needs: a real Supabase project, a Stripe test key and webhook secret, a Resend key, a seeded user per role.

Failure-sensitive notes. The Stripe webhook needs the raw body for signature verification and returns 5xx on an unknown session or customer so Stripe redelivers; a missing Stripe key gives a generic 503 payment_processor_unavailable. The digest send claims before it sends, so a same-day retry is idempotent; a missing Resend key logs resend_not_configured per recipient and does not crash. Auth emails (OTP, magic link) are sent by Supabase Auth, not Resend. A cron method mismatch fails as a silent 405.

No integration was found for Cloudflare R2, Sentry, PostHog or Redis, although the target's SRS names them.

Database configuration

  • Hosted Supabase Postgres, no ORM; types generated into lib/types/supabase.ts (bun run types:gen, needs the Supabase CLI through bunx and the project ref).
  • Migrations: 119 files NNNN_slug.sql (ordinal, not timestamp). They are applied through the Supabase MCP apply_migration tool, which writes the ledger; they are not applied with supabase db push. Rule in supabase/migrations/README.md: never run DDL through execute_sql.
  • No seed script or file exists.
  • QA tooling reaches the database through DBHub on the Session Pooler, port 5432 (not 6543), with the read-only role qa_inspector_ro (user form <user>.<project-ref>). Both QA roles (qa_inspector_ro, qa_inspector_rw) bypass RLS, and three secret tables are revoked from them. Credentials sit in a Jira Epic (BK-29), never in the repo.
  • The Supabase auth settings (OTP length, SMTP, rate limits, redirect allow-list) live only in the dashboard.

Local development recipe

Derived from package.json and the env files, because the target's README.md is the generic boilerplate README and has no run steps for Bunkai.

git clone https://github.com/upex-galaxy/upex-bunkai-tms.git
cd upex-bunkai-tms
git checkout staging          # the remote default branch
bun install                   # also runs `prepare` (husky)
cp .env.example .env          # fill values from the secret source
# ADD by hand: CRON_SECRET, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
# (the code requires them; the example file does not list them)
bun run dev                   # http://localhost:3000
curl http://localhost:3000/api/v1/health

Auth flow: the real requests

  • Password sign-in: POST /api/v1/auth/signin, public. JSON body: email (max 254), password (6 to 128), optional pat_name (1 to 80), pat_scopes, pat_expires_in_days (1 to 365). A failure is always 401 "Invalid email or password.".
  • Response 200: user (id, email), session (access_token, refresh_token, expires_at, token_type), pat (token shaped bk_pat_<prefix>.<secret>, id, name, scopes, expires_at) and a warning. The Supabase session cookie (sb-<project-ref>-auth-token) is set in the same response; the middleware refreshes it.
  • Sign-up: POST /api/v1/auth/signup (202, no session), then POST /api/v1/auth/confirm with the email OTP, which returns the session and PAT.
  • PAT use: header Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_<prefix>.<secret>; GET /api/v1/me shows the auth source and scopes. Cookie-only routes (POST and DELETE /tokens, POST /me/active-workspace) reject a Bearer with 403. workspace:admin is refused at sign-in.
  • Cron principal: Bearer <CRON_SECRET> for the two admin cron routes.
  • Health: GET /api/v1/health returns { ok, service, env, ts }; liveness only, no database check.

QA relevance: a seeded user per role does not exist, so test users come from sign-up plus confirm or from the Epic that holds the shared credentials.

Static assets, fonts, images

public/ holds only the generated openapi.json. Fonts load through next/font/google (Inter, JetBrains Mono, Noto Serif JP, display swap). next/image is not used; two raw <img> tags show run evidence because evidence arrives through an authorized redirect (components/runs/StepEvidence.tsx, components/runs/EvidenceLightbox.tsx).

Code splitting, bundle, performance

Dynamic imports appear only for the Monaco editor (components/atcs/AtcEditor.tsx, NewAtcEditor.tsx); 123 files are 'use client'. Only three loading.tsx files exist. No bundle analyzer, no web-vitals, no analytics or Vercel speed insights. Bundle size was not measured.

Routing, state and auth integration points

  • Route groups: (app) (protected shell with auth and chat providers) and (auth) (login). Public top-level routes: about, design-tokens, invites/accept, qa, workspaces/[id]/restore, auth/callback, auth/oauth/[provider], api/docs, api/openapi, api/v1/*.
  • Project pages live under (app)/projects/[projectSlug]/: atcs, bugs, metrics, milestones, plans, runs, settings, tests, traceability. Settings pages: account, billing, data-export, jira, notifications, tokens, workspaces.
  • Middleware matcher: /((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|.*\..*).*). Protected prefixes: /home, /projects, /onboarding, /settings, /activity, /atcs, /workspaces; unauthenticated users go to /login?next=.
  • Data: server components with RLS-scoped Supabase queries, Server Actions (for example app/(app)/atcs/actions.ts), REST under /api/v1 for PAT clients, and Supabase Realtime channels (run runner, sidebar, chat). State is React context only.
  • Error handling: no error.tsx, no global-error.tsx and no root not-found.tsx (only app/(app)/projects/[projectSlug]/not-found.tsx).

Test IDs strategy

About 1,157 data-testid= occurrences (895 unique literal values) in app/ and components/, pattern <area>-<element>[-<state>] in kebab-case. Samples: login-email (app/(auth)/login/email-first-form.tsx), login-signin (same file), atc-search-filter (app/(app)/projects/[projectSlug]/atc-search-filter.tsx), run-mode-badge (components/runs/RunModeBadge.tsx), bug-form-modal (components/bugs/BugFormDialog.tsx). The login page lists 13 ids on the /qa page. Caveat: login-email appears twice (also in magic-link-form.tsx), which breaks a strict Playwright locator once the magic-link toggle opens. Rule for this QA repo: ADR-0028.

Git flow

Main-integration: a feature or fix branch off staging merges into staging through a PR (--no-ff); a release promotes staging to main by fast-forward; a hotfix branches from main and is back-merged. Protected: main and staging.

Cloud services and database infrastructure

Vercel (hosting, cron), Supabase (Auth, Postgres, Realtime, Storage, Vault), Stripe, Resend; see external services. One hosted Supabase project; region, backups and the PostgreSQL version (the /qa page says 17) are not verifiable from the repo.

Monitoring and rollback

No error tracker, uptime monitor or analytics in code. The only runtime signal is the JSON access log (lib/api/logging.ts). No rollback procedure is documented in the repo; a Vercel rollback is a platform feature that was not verified. docs/workflows/environments.md is a generic tutorial.

QA relevance

  • Test accounts and data on staging are production data: prefix and clean up everything (ADR-0027).
  • A fresh .env built from the example file does not boot the app; the missing names are listed in backend.
  • A preview deploy reports itself as "staging" through getEnvironment().

CI/CD

CI platform: none. No .github/, .circleci/ or .gitlab-ci.yml. Nothing runs on the server before a merge. Docs mention .github/workflows and .context/ci-cd-setup.md in a generic way, but neither exists in the target. IaC: none (no Terraform, no supabase/config.toml). Docker: no Dockerfile or compose file; the "docker compose up" text in app/(auth)/login/page.tsx is marketing copy not backed by repo files.

Deployment

Vercel builds from Git (inferred; no .vercel folder or workflow proves it). vercel.json declares only the crons: /api/v1/admin/send-digest at 0 8 * * * and /api/v1/admin/storage-cleanup at 0 3 * * *. Vercel Cron calls with GET; both routes export GET and POST.

The only gates: local Husky hooks

HookWhat it runs
pre-commitlint-staged (eslint --fix on code, prettier on json, yml, css, html), then tsc --noEmit, vars:check, skills:check and conditional freshness checks; openapi:check when OpenAPI files are staged
pre-pushdocs:check, doc-contract lint, format:check, lint, env-variable parity (summarized from the file, not read in full), then bun scripts/openapi-gen.ts --check
commit-msgCommit-trailer check, warn only; no commitlint

No hook runs bun test. The hooks can be bypassed locally.

Release checklist

.context/release/README.md and pending-production-v2.md list the items to verify before promoting staging to main; bun run release:check runs their verify blocks. Pending entries include the magic-link rail (BK-400), the auth email rate limit, the OTP email copy, a missing version tag (0.1.0, no git tags) and an auth-config snapshot gap.

QA relevance

  • No CI test job exists to extend. This repo's suites run against staging on demand.
  • The Playwright suite for this project lives in the QA repo, not in the target.

Discovery gaps

  • Figure: the architecture section has no container diagram. It was not drawn in this pass; the component table and request-path steps carry the facts. Ask for one if wanted (it needs the diagram-design skill).
  • Runtime config not in the repo: Supabase and Vercel dashboard settings (OAuth providers, SMTP for auth emails, JWT expiry, redirect URLs, platform security headers). No supabase/config.toml.
  • Deployed schema: the repo only holds migration files (applied through the Supabase MCP, per supabase/migrations/README.md). Whether migration 0097 (evidence storage) is applied is unknown; the code header says it was not proven against a real bucket.
  • No measured figures: performance, uptime, error rate and coverage. Every numeric target above is an SRS claim or "unknown".
  • Stale target docs: the SRS non-functional spec says rate limiting is not implemented (it is, for check-email), and names R2, Sentry and PostHog (not in code). .context/SRS/api-contracts.yaml is design-time input, and its own header undercounts the live paths.
  • OpenAPI copies: public/openapi.json (110 paths, current by a script comparison) is the live contract. The copy at api/openapi.json has 78 paths and is stale. Only /api/v1/billing/webhook is absent from the live spec. A sync into this QA repo (bun run api:sync) should take the live one.
  • Env names disagree (code wins): .env.example advertises publishable and secret Supabase keys that no code reads, while lib/env.ts, middleware.ts and lib/supabase/server.ts require NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY. CRON_SECRET is required by lib/env.ts but absent from the example and both schemas. A fresh setup from the example file fails when lib/env.ts parses.
  • One database for all environments: the target's yaml sets one Supabase project ref for local, staging and production. The yaml is a claim; the deployed Vercel env values were not seen.
  • /qa page drift: it says "about 92 handlers" (the repo has 111 route.ts under app/api/v1), says PostgreSQL 17 (no supabase/config.toml to confirm), says the openapi and Postman MCPs are not declared by the repo while an openapi MCP exists in this environment, and names slots (API_BASE_URL, QA_INSPECTOR_*) that no schema declares. The target's README.md is the generic boilerplate README.
  • Deploy proof: Vercel Git integration, the branch-to-environment mapping and the staging alias are claims from the target's yaml; no .vercel folder, workflow or CI log proves them. Rollback and monitoring procedures: none found.
  • No seed: how test data and per-role users are provisioned is unknown beyond sign-up plus confirm and the credentials Epic (BK-29).
  • Versions: only ranges were read; resolved versions are in bun.lock. The middle of framework-gates.sh (lint and env-parity in pre-push) was summarized, not read in full.
  • Error boundaries: none exist (no error.tsx, global-error.tsx or root not-found.tsx), so an unhandled render error shows the framework default page. Not yet searched: whether any route besides check-email consumes the rate limiter; realtime channels and their RLS; accessibility tests; whether the 298 security definer lines equal that many functions; which ADR-0012 guard shapes each RPC follows.
